user.title: Which sensors measure what?
user.description: Solar Sanity checks that your energy figures add up, so it needs to know which sensor is which. Fields are pre-filled from your Energy Dashboard where possible — {found} were found. Consumption and generation are both required: without consumption the arithmetic closes by definition and cannot tell you anything.

data_description.pv: Power or energy produced by your panels.
data_description.grid_import: Power or energy drawn from the grid. If you have one sensor that goes negative when exporting, put it here and leave export empty.
data_description.grid_export: Power or energy sent to the grid.
data_description.battery_discharge: Energy coming out of the battery.
data_description.battery_soc_entity: Your battery's charge percentage, if you have it. It takes no part in the arithmetic. It is here for one job: if your battery's charge or discharge readings ever change abruptly, this is the only sensor that can say whether the battery changed or just the meter reporting it.

topology.title: A few things only you know
topology.description: Everything else is worked out from your data. Answer "Not sure" for anything you are unsure of — it is a real answer, and Solar Sanity will infer it rather than assume.

data.has_battery: Do you have a home battery?

data_description.load_whole_house: Answer "No" if it only covers a backup or critical-loads panel.

overlap.title: That sensor is already being watched
overlap.description:
{entity_id} is already mapped by “{other}”.

If this is the same installation, go back and set it up once — you can change any of its sensors afterwards with Reconfigure, without losing history. If these really are two separate systems that share a meter, carry on.

error.load_required: A consumption sensor is required. Without one the balance closes by definition and Solar Sanity cannot check anything.
error.duplicate_entity: The same sensor is mapped to two different roles. One sensor cannot be on both sides of the calculation — it would cancel itself out.
error.load_already_monitored: Another Solar Sanity installation already measures consumption with this sensor, so the two describe the same house. Reconfigure that one instead — every sensor it uses can be changed without losing any history.

data_description.guaranteed_annual_kwh: The yearly figure your installer promised, if you have it. Compared against what you actually produced, once there is a full year of history to compare.
data_description.suppressed_codes: Anything ticked here will not be raised again. Only findings this installation has actually been given are listed, and a dismissal can be undone by unticking it.
data_description.battery_soc_entity: Optional. Your battery's state of charge, as a percentage. It takes no part in the energy arithmetic — it is there for one job: if your battery's charge or discharge readings ever change abruptly, this is the only sensor that can say whether the battery changed or just the meter reporting it.
